slides.texte_overlay:
tiny habits that make every
morning feel like a reset

stretching before screens

spend two minutes stretching before you check anything at all. a stiff body makes a stiff mind, and those two minutes change how the whole first hour of your day feels.

open the curtains first

open the curtains or step outside within five minutes of waking up. daylight tells your body the day has started, and you feel awake much faster than with screens.

one lesson with breakfast

spend 5 minutes over breakfast learning one new thing: a planet, a painter, a moment in history. starting the day curious sets a completely different tone than starting it stressed.

slides.texte_overlay:
making the bed

make your bed as soon as you get up. it takes a minute, it's the first finished task of your day, and coming home to it at night feels like a small gift to yourself.

three lines on paper

write three lines on paper before you touch your phone: how you feel, what matters today, one thing you look forward to. it puts you in charge of the day.
